title: How old your cells are, by type (days)

source.name: Carbon-14 birth dating of human cells (Jonas Frisen, Karolinska Institute)
source.publisher: Peer-reviewed cell biology research, as compiled in mainstream science coverage

notes: Carbon-14 dating studies (pioneered by Jonas Frisen's lab) found that neurons in the cerebral cortex are essentially as old as the person -- they are not meaningfully replaced across a lifetime, so their 'age' is shown here as roughly a full lifespan (~80 years = ~29,200 days). Skin's outer layer, by contrast, fully renews roughly every 28 days.
